This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: ANSWER ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: ANSWER ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: ANSWER 2 QUESTIONS OUT OF 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0, Mg = 24.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 $\mathrm{cm^3}$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 $\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,{}^{\circ}C^{-1}}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 273\ \mathrm{K}$.
enonce_intro_markdown:
This question concerns some organic compounds belonging to different homologous series.

**A:** $\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}$ **B:** $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ **C:** $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ **D:** $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$
incertitudes: Q4(b)(ii) : « at rtp » imprimé ; le corrigé précise que la substitution de l'éthane exige la lumière (UV).

questions.enonce_markdown: What is a homologous series? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: A homologous series is a **family of organic compounds with the same general formula and the same functional group**, so similar chemical properties; successive members differ by a $-\mathrm{CH_2}-$ unit and their physical properties change gradually.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select from A to D:

(i) an unsaturated compound

(ii) a compound that readily undergoes substitution reaction with halogens at rtp *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **C** ($\mathrm{C_2H_4}$, ethene): it has a carbon-carbon double bond.

(ii) **D** ($\mathrm{C_2H_6}$, ethane): alkanes are saturated and react with halogens by substitution (a hydrogen atom is replaced by a halogen, e.g. $\mathrm{C_2H_6 + Cl_2 \rightarrow C_2H_5Cl + HCl}$), in diffuse light or ultraviolet light.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Compounds A and B react in the presence of concentrated Sulphuric acid.

(i) Write an equation for the reaction.

(ii) Identify the family of organic compounds to which the main product belongs. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A is propanol ($\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}$) and B is ethanoic acid ($\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$): this is **esterification**.

(i) $\mathrm{CH_3COOH + C_3H_7OH \rightleftharpoons CH_3COOC_3H_7 + H_2O}$ (conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ as catalyst and dehydrating agent, heat).

Check: left C 5, H 12, O 3; right C 5, H 10 + 2 = 12, O 2 + 1 = 3. Balanced.

(ii) The main product, propyl ethanoate, belongs to the **esters**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Give the different structural forms of compound A

(ii) How are these structural forms called? *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Compound A, $\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}$, has two structural forms:

- propan-1-ol: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2OH}$ (the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group is on the end carbon);

- propan-2-ol: $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3}$ (the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group is on the middle carbon).

(ii) They are called **structural isomers** (more precisely, position isomers): same molecular formula, different structural formulae.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the reagent that is used to distinguish compound C from compound D and state the observation. Reagent: ... Observation: ... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reagent:** bromine water (aqueous bromine) - acidified potassium manganate(VII) also works.

**Observation:** with C (ethene) the orange-brown bromine water is **decolourised** (an addition reaction takes place); with D (ethane) the orange-brown colour is unchanged. With acidified potassium manganate(VII), ethene turns the purple solution colourless and ethane does not.
